_note: The sector layer. Nothing is authored here that no exhibit renders, because this repository has already learned once what happens to a data file that renders on no page. Every figure is a research house projection, an industry estimate or a government estimate and is tagged SECONDARY, with one exception: the peer benchmarking table is read out of a filing and carries its printed page. No currency is converted anywhere in this file. Dollar figures stay dollars and rupee figures stay rupees, the same way the company files keep one filer in rupees beside another in dollars, and the only unit both halves of this page share is the megawatt.

indiaAI._note: The government scheme that handed ten providers a deadline, which makes it the one place a reader can watch announcement and execution separate at provider level. The brief gives one provider's offer and a national installed total, not a per provider deployment table, so no per provider installed figure is recorded here and none is drawn. Status is what has been publicly reported about each, and five of the ten have nothing reported either way.

hyperscalers._note: Three foreign firms, three announcements, one country. Each pledge is stated in dollars over a horizon of four to five years, and the estate they are pledged into is measured in megawatts, so nothing here is set against anything it cannot honestly be compared with. The money is compared with money: the annual size of the market being pledged into, and the commitment the whole sector has already recorded. The capacity is compared with capacity: the single announcement that named one, against what the country operates. Two of the three named no capacity at all, and that is carried as null rather than guessed.

power._note: Electricity demand, which is not the quantity the capacity forecasts above are stated in. Those are IT load, the power the servers themselves draw. This is grid demand, which includes everything the building spends to keep those servers running and cool. The two are never converted into one another on this page, because the conversion is a facility level efficiency figure and nothing in this repository has read one.
power.currentNote: Data centre electricity demand today, approximately, across the whole national estate.

source.label: Ministry of Power estimate of data centre electricity demand, as carried in the project brief. Unlike the transmission delay dataset this project pulled from the ministry directly, this figure has not been traced to the ministry's own publication.

unitEconomics._note: What a megawatt costs to build and what it costs to run. Industry ranges rather than any one operator's figures, which is why they sit in the sector file and not in a company file. The capital cost per megawatt is what turns a capacity forecast into a capital requirement, and it is the only figure here that anything derives from.

source.label: Colocation unit economics. Capital cost per megawatt from CareEdge, the margin range and the cost split from industry commentary, both as carried in the project brief.

operatorReturns._note: The only primary figures on this page. Eight data centre operators, five Indian and three global, with return on capital and depreciation rate for three fiscal years, printed as a single table inside the prospectus industry report. NA in the source is carried as null and drawn as an absence, never as a zero.

claim.quote: Sify achieved ROCE of 9.88%, 6.75% and 7.92% in Fiscal 2023, Fiscal 2024 and Fiscal 2025, respectively, which is significantly higher than its global peers.

issuerReason.quote: Sify's depreciation rose from INR 2,083.00 million in Fiscal 2023 to INR 3,268.16 million in Fiscal 2025, resulting in a depreciation rate of 10.33% in Fiscal 2025 the highest among its peers. This partly weighed on its ROCE.

source.label: Sify Infinit Spaces DRHP, peer benchmarking table inside the commissioned 1Lattice and Cushman and Wakefield industry report. Return on capital employed is EBIT over average capital employed, on the definition printed on the following page. Fiscal years are the Indian convention, ending 31 March. The two largest global names carry a footnote in the source marking a different reporting basis.
